summary.one_liner: sqlparse is a non-validating SQL parser for Python that splits scripts into statements, formats SQL, and exposes a token tree for inspection.
summary.what_it_does: It tokenizes SQL text and groups recognized parts into a tree of statements, clauses, identifiers and expressions. It accepts input without validating it and makes no assumptions about a specific SQL dialect, so vendor extensions and templated SQL can be parsed. The module-level functions split() (divide a script into statements), format() (reindent, change keyword case, strip comments, set indent width, and similar options) and parse() (return a statement tree) cover most uses. It also installs a sqlformat command-line tool that reads stdin or files and can rewrite files in place. A pre-commit hook for sqlformat is documented.
use_cases: split a SQL script into individual statements
format SQL files on commit with pre-commit
walk the token tree of a SQL statement
build a linter or query analysis tool
how_to_run: import sqlparse; sqlparse.split("select * from foo; select * from bar;")
notable: Non-validating parser that accepts any input, so vendor extensions and templated SQL parse
Dialect-agnostic tokenizer and grouping into a navigable token tree
Provides both a Python API and the sqlformat command-line tool
Pre-commit hook integration for formatting SQL files
Parts of the code are based on Pygments
caveats: Non-validating: it does not check that SQL is correct
Maintained in spare time, so issue and pull request replies can be slow
